Sony MSM8996 v3 GCC/MMCC digital voltage coupling
================================================

The native qcom,gcc-msm8996 and qcom,mmcc-msm8996 controllers can use the
final Sony MSM8996 v3 frequency-to-corner plans. Dora requires this mode;
it is also selected explicitly by sony,msm8996-voltage-coupling.

Required properties when coupling is selected:
- vdd-dig-supply: typed logical-corner regulator for PM8994 S1/CX, provided
  by qcom,msm8996-rpm-corner-resource with resource-name "smpa", id 1.
  The child must cover ACTIVE and SLEEP sets (qcom,set = <3>).
- For MMCC only:
  - mmpll4-dig-supply: another consumer of that same S1 corner regulator.
  - mmpll4-analog-supply: physical PM8994 L12 regulator, exactly 1800000 uV.

Optional property:
- sony,msm8996-voltage-coupling: boolean enabling these Sony v3 contracts on
  an explicitly audited board. It does not describe unrelated SoC revisions.

Do not connect vdd-dig or mmpll4-dig to a physical microvolt regulator or
dummy supply. Consumers issue logical corner 1/3/4/5/7 for source levels
NONE/LOWER/LOW/NOMINAL/HIGH; only the typed provider translates wire values.

Controllers must be built in. Probe obtains a real ACKed HIGH lease before
clock hardware writes. CCF retains the highest-corner handoff until unused
clocks have been parked and boot clock ownership/rates are known. Unknown
boot-active parents retain HIGH and prohibit lowering. Probe retries reuse
one bounded device reference and consumer lease; a failed probe does not
release the voltage of unknown firmware clocks. Manual bind/unbind is not
offered. The retained reference also covers dynamic platform removal.
Deferred probes after the global handoff still acquire a tracked HIGH lease.
Any enabled raw PLL lacking a prepared main-output owner retains HIGH too.
Only complete clock ownership can release that lease; failed release retains
the recorded vote. This may conservatively keep HIGH after early cleanup.

The raw *_EARLY PLLs remain internal parents on a coupled board; their DT
numeric IDs are not exported, since the source limits describe main outputs,
not raw VCO frequencies. Use the regulated main-output and source clocks.
GPLL0 main remains read-only, critical and observed at the source 600 MHz;
an unexpected firmware rate fails probe without reprogramming the root.

L12 is an ordinary physical RPM rail. Any voltage/enable/disable error makes
the analog class uncertain and permanently quarantines further PLL operations;
a cached consumer enable count cannot recover a lost physical SWEN ACK.
Physical L12 SLEEP programming and suspend/resume require separate validation.

Example:
  &gcc {
      sony,msm8996-voltage-coupling;
      vdd-dig-supply = <&pm8994_s1_corner>;
  };
  &mmcc {
      sony,msm8996-voltage-coupling;
      vdd-dig-supply = <&pm8994_s1_corner>;
      mmpll4-dig-supply = <&pm8994_s1_corner>;
      mmpll4-analog-supply = <&pm8994_l12>;
  };
